Main set

#1word-bankfrom Q1inquiry 7.2
A model of refraction uses expanding secondary wavelets to build successive wavefronts, and correctly predicts that light slows down and bends towards the normal when it enters a denser medium. This wave model of light was proposed by ___.
A model of refraction uses expanding secondary wavelets to build successive wavefronts, and correctly predicts that light slows down and bends towards the normal when it enters a denser medium. This wave model of light was proposed by Huygens.
Word bank
Huygens Newton Planck Malus Maxwell
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): Newton's competing model treated light as particles that speed up in a denser medium.
#2true-falsefrom Q1binquiry 7.2
Newton's particle (corpuscular) model of light predicted that light travels faster in a denser medium such as glass than it does in air.
  • ✓ True
  • False
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): This prediction was later shown to be wrong; light travels slower in a denser medium, as the wave model predicts.
#3true-falsefrom Q2inquiry 6.4
An AC induction motor requires brushes (or slip rings) to supply current directly to its rotor.
  • True
  • ✓ False
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): The rotor current in an induction motor is induced by the stator's rotating magnetic field, with no direct electrical connection to the rotor.
#4word-bankfrom Q2binquiry 6.4
An AC induction motor needs a stator winding and magnetic fields to work, but unlike a DC motor it does not need ___ to make an electrical connection to its rotor.
An AC induction motor needs a stator winding and magnetic fields to work, but unlike a DC motor it does not need brushes to make an electrical connection to its rotor.
Word bank
brushes a stator magnetic fields an iron core
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): The rotor current is induced by the stator's rotating field, so the rotor has no electrical contacts at all.
#5multiple-choicefrom Q3inquiry 7.1
What was the basis for Maxwell's prediction of the speed of electromagnetic waves?
  • ✓ His equations describing how oscillating electric and magnetic fields propagate through space
  • Experiments using light and mirrors to measure the finite speed of light
  • Experiments using magnetic fields to accelerate charged particles
  • Equations describing how electromagnetic waves are bent by gravitational fields
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): Maxwell's equations gave a wave speed of $1/\sqrt{\mu_0 \varepsilon_0}$, which matched the measured speed of light.
#6numeric-entryfrom Q4inquiry 8.4
The mass of a radioactive isotope falls from 400 g to 200 g over 100 years. Calculate its decay constant $\lambda$, using $\lambda = \dfrac{\ln 2}{t_{1/2}}$.
0.00693yr^{-1}
accepted within ±3% (relative)
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): The mass halving in 100 years means the half-life is 100 years.
#7numeric-entryfrom Q4binquiry 8.4
A radioactive sample starts with a mass of 400 g and has a half-life of 100 years. Calculate the time taken for the sample to decay to 100 g.
200years
accepted within ±2% (relative)
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): 400 g to 100 g is two halvings.
#8true-falsefrom Q5inquiry 5.1
A ball is thrown and follows a parabolic path with negligible air resistance. Decreasing only the vertical component of the launch velocity would make the ball's time of flight shorter.
  • ✓ True
  • False
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): Time of flight depends only on the vertical motion; a smaller upward velocity means less time in the air.
#9word-bankfrom Q6inquiry 8.1
2020-q6-cluster-hr-diagram.png
The stars plotted on the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram shown all belong to one globular cluster. They have approximately the same ___.
The stars plotted on the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram shown all belong to one globular cluster. They have approximately the same age.
Word bank
age colour luminosity mass surface temperature
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): The stars of a cluster all formed together from the same gas cloud, but with a range of masses.
#10true-falsefrom Q6binquiry 8.1
2020-q6-cluster-hr-diagram.png
The point where a globular cluster's main sequence bends away towards the giant branch (the 'main-sequence turnoff') is used to estimate the cluster's age.
  • ✓ True
  • False
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): More massive stars leave the main sequence first, so the mass at the turnoff tells you how long the cluster has existed.
#11multiple-choicefrom Q7inquiry 6.2
2020-q7-output-waveform.png
A device produces the voltage output shown: a series of identical positive humps (pulsating direct current). Which device produces this output?
  • ✓ A generator connected to the external circuit through a split-ring commutator (a DC generator)
  • A generator connected to the external circuit through two slip rings (an AC generator)
  • A transformer with an AC supply on the primary coil
  • A DC electric motor
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): A split-ring commutator reverses the connections every half turn, folding the negative half of each cycle up into a positive hump.
#12true-falsefrom Q7binquiry 6.2
Replacing the split-ring commutator of a simple DC generator with two slip rings would change its output from pulsating DC to alternating current.
  • ✓ True
  • False
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): Slip rings keep each end of the coil permanently connected to the same output terminal, so the reversing EMF appears at the output.
#13drag-dropfrom Q8inquiry 8.4
2020-q8-decay-nz-plot.png
A uranium isotope U (atomic number 92, 146 neutrons) undergoes four successive decays, ending at product Q, as plotted on the neutron number versus atomic number diagram shown. Step R is the last decay, from (Z = 92, N = 142) to Q at (Z = 90, N = 140). Match each label to the correct entry.
Process R→Alpha decay
Product Q→$^{230}_{90}$Th (thorium-230)
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): Step R lowers Z by 2 and N by 2, which is alpha decay. Q has Z = 90 and mass number 90 + 140 = 230.
#14true-falsefrom Q8binquiry 8.4
2020-q8-decay-nz-plot.png
On the decay diagram shown, the first step goes from U at (Z = 92, N = 146) to a nuclide at (Z = 90, N = 144). Because both the atomic number and the neutron number decrease by 2, this step is an alpha decay.
  • ✓ True
  • False
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): An alpha particle is 2 protons and 2 neutrons.
#15true-falsefrom Q8cinquiry 8.4
In a beta-minus decay, the atomic number of the nucleus increases by 1 while its neutron number decreases by 1.
  • ✓ True
  • False
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): A neutron converts to a proton, emitting an electron and an antineutrino.
#16multiple-choicefrom Q9inquiry 8.3
Which observation provided evidence supporting Bohr's improvement to Rutherford's model of the atom?
  • ✓ Each element produces a unique emission spectrum made up of discrete wavelengths
  • A small percentage of alpha particles fired at a gold foil were deflected by more than 90 degrees
  • A beam of electrons reflected from a nickel crystal produced a diffraction pattern
  • An electron and a positron annihilated to produce two photons travelling in opposite directions
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): Discrete spectral lines are explained by electrons dropping between fixed (quantised) energy levels.
#17drag-dropfrom Q10inquiry 6.1
2020-q10-charged-plates.png
An electron enters the region between two charged plates travelling horizontally to the right, and curves downward towards the bottom plate, as shown. A magnetic field is then added so that a second identical electron passes straight through undeflected. Match each field to its direction.
Direction of the electric field between the plates→Towards the top of the page
Direction of the magnetic field that lets the second electron pass straight through→Out of the page
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): The electron curves down, so the electric force on it is downward and the field (opposite for a negative charge) points up. The magnetic force must then point up to cancel it.
#18true-falsefrom Q10binquiry 6.1
2020-q10-charged-plates.png
In the setup shown, the first electron curves towards the bottom plate, so the electric force on it points downward and the electric field between the plates points upward (towards the top plate).
  • ✓ True
  • False
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): For a negative charge, the electric force is opposite to the field direction.
#19multiple-choicefrom Q11inquiry 8.4
In the reaction $^{6}_{3}\mathrm{Li} + ^{1}_{0}\mathrm{n} \rightarrow ^{4}_{2}\mathrm{He} + ^{3}_{1}\mathrm{H}$, the total mass of the reactants is 7.023787704 u and the total mass of the products is 7.018652532 u. What type of reaction is this?
  • ✓ A transmutation in which energy is released
  • A transmutation that requires an input of energy
  • A fusion reaction in which energy is released
  • A fusion reaction that requires an input of energy
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): The products are lighter than the reactants, so mass has been converted to energy. One element has changed into others, which is transmutation (not fusion).
#20numeric-entryfrom Q11binquiry 8.4
For the reaction in the previous question, the reactant mass is 7.023787704 u and the product mass is 7.018652532 u. Calculate the energy released. Take 1 u = 931.5 MeV/$c^2$.
4.78MeV
accepted within ±3% (relative)
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): Energy released = (mass lost in u) $\times$ 931.5 MeV.
#21word-bankfrom Q12inquiry 5.3
The escape velocity from Earth for an object depends only on the object's distance from Earth's centre, not on its mass. Of four satellites at distances of $r$, $2r$, $3r$ and $4r$ from Earth's centre, the one with the greatest escape velocity is the one at distance ___.
The escape velocity from Earth for an object depends only on the object's distance from Earth's centre, not on its mass. Of four satellites at distances of $r$, $2r$, $3r$ and $4r$ from Earth's centre, the one with the greatest escape velocity is the one at distance $r$.
Word bank
$r$ $2r$ $3r$ $4r$
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): $v_{esc} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM_{Earth}}{d}}$, which is largest when $d$ is smallest.
#22numeric-entryfrom Q12cinquiry 5.3
Calculate the escape velocity from the surface of Earth. Take Earth's mass as $5.97 \times 10^{24}$ kg, Earth's radius as $6.37 \times 10^{6}$ m, and $G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11}$ N m$^2$ kg$^{-2}$.
11200m s^{-1}
accepted within ±3% (relative)
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): $v_{esc} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{r}}$.
#23multiple-choicefrom Q13inquiry 7.3
2020-q13-photoelectric-graph.png
Light of frequency $8 \times 10^{14}$ Hz is used to irradiate both metals whose photoelectric response is shown. Metal Y has a higher threshold frequency than metal X. Compared with the photoelectrons emitted from metal X, the photoelectrons emitted from metal Y will:
  • ✓ have a lower maximum velocity
  • have a higher maximum velocity
  • take a longer time to gain enough energy to be ejected
  • be ejected sooner
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): At the same frequency, the metal with the higher threshold frequency gives its photoelectrons less kinetic energy.
#24word-bankfrom Q13binquiry 7.3
2020-q13-photoelectric-graph.png
On a graph of maximum photoelectron kinetic energy against the frequency of the incident light, the gradient of the straight line is equal to ___.
On a graph of maximum photoelectron kinetic energy against the frequency of the incident light, the gradient of the straight line is equal to Planck's constant.
Word bank
Planck's constant the work function the threshold frequency the speed of light
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): The photoelectric equation is $E_{k,max} = hf - \phi$, a straight line of gradient $h$.
#25true-falsefrom Q13cinquiry 7.3
Because metal Y has a higher threshold frequency than metal X, metal Y also has a larger work function.
  • ✓ True
  • False
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): Work function $\phi = h f_0$, where $f_0$ is the threshold frequency.
#26drag-dropfrom Q14inquiry 6.2
Two long parallel wires X and Y initially carry equal currents in the same direction, and the force on each wire has magnitude $F$ (attractive). The current in wire Y is then doubled and reversed in direction (the current in X is unchanged). Match each change to its effect on the force on wire X.
Doubling the current in wire Y→The force magnitude doubles, to $2F$
Reversing the direction of the current in wire Y→The attraction becomes a repulsion
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): The force is proportional to the product of the currents, and its sign depends on whether the currents are parallel or antiparallel.
#27word-bankfrom Q14binquiry 6.2
The force per unit length between two parallel current-carrying wires is ___ proportional to the product of the two currents, so doubling one of the currents ___ the force.
The force per unit length between two parallel current-carrying wires is directly proportional to the product of the two currents, so doubling one of the currents doubles the force.
Word bank
directly inversely doubles halves quadruples
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): $\dfrac{F}{\ell} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2\pi d}$.
#28multiple-choicefrom Q15inquiry 5.1
A rocket of mass 7800 kg is travelling horizontally at 20 m s$^{-1}$, oriented nose-up with its engine exhaust pointing downward. The engine thrust is set to 90 000 N (vertically upward). Taking $g = 9.8$ m s$^{-2}$, which best describes its subsequent motion?
  • ✓ It keeps moving sideways while accelerating upward, following a path that curves upward
  • It follows a downward parabolic path like a projectile
  • It continues in a straight horizontal line at constant velocity
  • It stops moving sideways and rises vertically
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): Weight is $7800 \times 9.8 \approx 76\,400$ N, less than the 90 000 N thrust, so there is a net upward force while the horizontal velocity is unchanged.
#29numeric-entryfrom Q15binquiry 5.1
For the 7800 kg rocket in the previous question, with 90 000 N of upward thrust and $g = 9.8$ m s$^{-2}$, calculate the magnitude of its vertical acceleration immediately after the thrust change.
1.74m s^{-2}
accepted within ±4% (relative)
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): $a = \dfrac{F_{thrust} - mg}{m}$.
#30multiple-choicefrom Q16inquiry 8.4
2020-q16-reactor-core.png
In a fission reactor core, the moderator slows neutrons to increase the rate of fission, the control rods absorb free neutrons, and the coolant removes heat. A fault causes some of the moderator to leak out of the core. Which action would best compensate for the loss of moderator?
  • ✓ Withdraw the control rods further out of the core
  • Lower the control rods further into the core
  • Pump the coolant through the core at a faster rate
  • Reduce the temperature of the coolant before pumping it in
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): Less moderator means fewer neutrons are slowed to fission-causing speeds, so the reaction rate falls; removing neutron-absorbing control rods pushes it back up.
#31drag-dropfrom Q16binquiry 8.4
2020-q16-reactor-core.png
Match each component of the fission reactor core shown to its function.
Moderator→Slows down neutrons so they are more likely to cause further fission
Control rods→Absorb neutrons to regulate the rate of the chain reaction
Coolant→Carries heat away from the core
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): Only the control rods are adjusted during normal operation to speed up or slow down the reaction.
#32multiple-choicefrom Q17inquiry 7.4
2020-q17-relativity-train.png
Observer X is on a train moving at a constant 0.95c relative to the ground. Observer Y stands on the ground. As X passes Y, X sends a short light pulse towards a sensor at the front of the carriage. Which statement is correct?
  • ✓ X measures a longer time for the pulse to reach the sensor than Y does
  • Y measures the speed of the pulse to be 0.05c
  • X measures a shorter distance for the pulse to travel than Y does
  • X and Y measure the same distance and the same travel time
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): The speed of light is c for both observers, but they disagree on the distance and time; working through the Lorentz transformation gives a longer time in X's frame here.
#33true-falsefrom Q17binquiry 7.4
Both observer X (on the train) and observer Y (on the ground) measure the speed of the light pulse to be $c$.
  • ✓ True
  • False
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): The constancy of the speed of light for all inertial observers is Einstein's second postulate.
#34word-bankfrom Q18inquiry 5.3
2020-q18-io-romer.png
An observer times one orbit of Io around Jupiter while Earth moves between each labelled pair of points (P, Q, R and S) on its orbit, as shown. The measured orbital period of Io is longest for the pair at point ___.
An observer times one orbit of Io around Jupiter while Earth moves between each labelled pair of points (P, Q, R and S) on its orbit, as shown. The measured orbital period of Io is longest for the pair at point Q.
Word bank
P Q R S
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): The measured period is longest where Earth is moving away from Jupiter during the measurement, so light from the end of the orbit has further to travel than light from the start.
#35true-falsefrom Q18binquiry 5.3
When Earth is moving away from Jupiter during a measurement of Io's orbital period, the period appears longer than its true value because light from the end of the orbit has to travel a greater distance to reach Earth.
  • ✓ True
  • False
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): This effect was used by Romer to make the first estimate of the speed of light.
#36multiple-choicefrom Q19inquiry 6.3
2020-q19-rotating-conductor.png
A straight conductor PQ rotates at constant angular velocity about the end P, in a plane that contains a uniform magnetic field B. At the instant shown, PQ is perpendicular to B. Which best describes the induced EMF between P and Q over one complete revolution?
  • ✓ It varies sinusoidally, starting from zero and completing one full cycle
  • It varies sinusoidally, starting from its maximum value
  • It stays at zero throughout
  • It decreases at a steady rate
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): When PQ is perpendicular to B (as shown) the conductor moves parallel to the field lines and cuts no flux, so the EMF is momentarily zero.
#37multiple-choicefrom Q20inquiry 5.2
2020-q20-semicircular-wall.png
A ball is launched with velocity u at an angle to the horizontal and follows a path around the inside of a smooth (frictionless), vertical, semicircular wall of radius r, as shown. It does not reach the top of the wall and lands on the ground opposite its starting point. Which statement correctly describes the net force on the ball during its motion?
  • ✓ The magnitude of the net force remains constant
  • The direction of the net force is always vertically downward
  • The direction of the net force is always perpendicular to the wall
  • The magnitude of the net force is smallest when the ball is at its highest point
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): The wall is smooth, so it does no work on the ball: the horizontal speed stays constant, which makes the (horizontal) normal force constant in magnitude, and gravity is already constant.
#38drag-dropfrom Q20binquiry 5.2
2020-q20-semicircular-wall.png
For the ball moving around the inside of the smooth semicircular wall shown, match each part of its motion to the correct description.
Vertical motion of the ball→Free fall: acceleration is g downward the whole time
Horizontal motion of the ball→Circular motion around the axis at constant speed
💡 Tip (shown only if the student answers incorrectly): The normal force is horizontal, so it never affects the vertical motion and never does work on the horizontal motion.
